# Actions and menus

> Settled 2026-09-09. Answers `analysis/ui/ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md` §§ 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.

## 1. The kebab

**Horizontal, everywhere.** One icon: Hugeicons' `MoreHorizontalIcon` (since 2026-11-04; it was
lucide's `MoreHorizontal`). The product once had a horizontal, a vertical and a second name for the
same glyph, so moving between `/settings/people/roles` and `/settings/general/job-catalog` changed the
control for the same job. `RowActionsMenu` is the one way to draw it.

```tsx
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Row actions">
  <Icon icon={MoreHorizontalIcon} size="sm" />
</Button>
```

`aria-label` is **not optional** — an icon-only button with no label is an unlabelled button to a
screen reader, and two of the nineteen shipped without one.

## 2. Inside the menu

**Every item has an icon.** Not "the modules that already do" — every item, everywhere. An icon set
that stops halfway reads as a rendering bug rather than a style.

```tsx
<RowAction icon={<Icon icon={PencilEdit02Icon} size="sm" />} onClick={rename}>
  Rename
</RowAction>
```

**Destructive items are red and separated** (SPEC § 4.6). A separator above, `RowActionDestructive`
(or `variant="destructive"` on a plain item) — not a hand-written red, of which the product had three
spellings. The
separator is the point as much as the colour: it is the pause between "the things you do to this
row" and "the thing you cannot undo".

```tsx
<RowActionDestructive icon={<Icon icon={Delete02Icon} size="sm" />} onClick={remove}>
  Delete
</RowActionDestructive>
```

**Only genuinely destructive items get this.** Archive is not destructive — it is reversible by
decision (`DECISIONS.md` § "Every archive is reversible") — so it is an ordinary item. One menu put
the separator before **Archive**, which is what happens when the separator means "near the bottom"
instead of "past this line it is permanent".

## 3. Size

SPEC § 13.7 since 2026-11-04: a menu is radius 10, level 2, 4 px padding; an item is 32 px high,
radius 8, `accent-subtle` on hover. `RowActionsMenu` and the kit's `DropdownMenu` draw exactly that.

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Content | `w-40 rounded-popover p-1 shadow-popover` (the kit's default) |
| Item | `h-8 gap-2.5 rounded-control px-2.5` (the kit's default) |
| Item icon | `<Icon size="sm" />`, `text-tertiary` |
| Trigger | `variant="ghost" size="icon-sm"` |

The product had four widths (`w-40`, `w-44`, `w-56`, Radix default), three trigger sizes and two item
paddings. These numbers are now the only ones.

**§§ 1–3 are one component: `RowActionsMenu`.** Use it rather than composing the pieces. Its
**destructive slot renders its own separator**, which is the only way to make "separator above, red,
one spelling" true by construction rather than by review — the product had four spellings, and three
menus styled Delete exactly like Rename.

## 4. The page toolbar

Every list page and every table has the same bar, in the same order.

```
[ Search ]  [ Filter ]                          [ Show archived ]  [ secondary ]  [ + Add Thing ]
└──────── left group ────────┘                  └──────────── right group ────────────┘
```

- **Search is always leftmost**, and **Filter follows it** where the screen has one. Nothing else
  goes in the left group.
- **Action buttons are right**, primary last.
- **The archived toggle is the leftmost element of the right group** — see § 5.

The bar is `ListToolbar`. **Tabs are not part of it**: where a page has tabs choosing *which* list,
they are their own row above the toolbar, which acts on the list chosen — the roles page was reshaped
this way because its tabs sat where search belongs.

**Screens that are not list pages keep their own layout** and take only the search box: the People
topbar (a column picker, a view manager and a filter builder), the documents toolbar, the canvas
toolbars, and the panels inside a detail page.

### The search box

The reference is the public-holidays one, with more air around the icon:

```tsx
<SearchBox value={q} onChange={setQ} />   {/* components/ui/SearchBox: 260 px, the icon, the word "Search" */}
```

**The placeholder is the word `Search`. Nothing else.** Not `Search calendars`, not `Search people…`,
not `Search templates...` — the product had those and more, differing in the noun and in whether the
ellipsis was a character or three dots. The field sits inside a screen that already says what it
lists; repeating the noun buys nothing and guarantees drift.

It is `components/ui/SearchBox`, at exactly that geometry, with Escape to clear. **The placeholder is not
a prop**, so it cannot drift again. **`SearchField` is a different control** — the canvas search, with a
mode switch, a match counter and prev/next arrows — and is not to be merged into it: one component
with eight props, six of them always undefined, is two components pretending.

## 5. Show archived

**A toggle between two views, not a widening of one.** On: **only** archived records. Off: everything
else. The product had it as an additive "also show archived", drawn three different ways, with the
label flipping to "Hide archived" on two screens.

**It is not rendered when nothing is archived.** A toggle that switches to an empty list is a control
that cannot work, and § 2 of the README says those are absent rather than dead. This means the screen
needs the archived count, not just the archived rows.

Position: leftmost in the right-hand group.

The component is `ArchivedToggle`, and **it takes a count, not a boolean** — deliberately: a caller that
only knows "there are some" cannot obey the hide-when-empty rule, so asking for the number forces each
list to be able to answer it. A list that holds its rows client-side counts locally; **a list that pages
from the server needs its endpoint to return the archived count**.

## 6. The add button

**`+ Add <thing>`, always.** `Add Office`, `Add Role`, `Add Legal Entity`, `Add Policy`,
`Add Calendar`. Never `Create …`.

The product had `Create role` and `Add Office` on two tabs of the same page, and a modal whose submit
button then said **Create** — so the user pressed Add and confirmed Create. The submit button inside
the modal follows the same verb: **Add**.

```tsx
<Button>
  <Icon icon={Add01Icon} size="sm" />
  Add office
</Button>
```

The button spaces its icon itself (`gap-2`); an icon inside a button carries no margin. Capitalisation
is sentence case, per [`NAMING.md`](NAMING.md).

## 7. Which actions confirm

**These five always open a modal**, on every screen, without exception:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Archive** | reversible, but it removes the record from where people expect it |
| **Delete** | |
| **Unassign** | |
| **Remove** | |
| **Duplicate** | it creates something, and a copy made by accident is found much later |

Everything else fires immediately: Activate, Unarchive, Rename (its own dialog is the edit form, not
a confirmation), Star, Deactivate.

**Why Duplicate is on the list.** It is the only non-destructive member, and it is there because its
failure mode is silence: an accidental duplicate looks exactly like a deliberate one, and nobody
notices until somebody edits the wrong copy.

The state before this rule: Archive confirmed on five screens and fired immediately on two — one of
them **with no error handling at all**, so a refused archive was completely silent. Unassign
confirmed on roles and was a hover-only ✕ on the department and team tabs, unreachable on touch.

The dialog is `ConfirmActionModal`. **It stays open while the action runs and while it fails**, so a
refusal is written inside the dialog that asked, per the error formula — the defect
`DeleteDocumentsFolderModal` carries a comment about.

## What this does not settle

- **Confirm *and* undo on the same act.** Archiving a time off policy both confirms and offers the undo
  toast (`DECISIONS.md` § "Every archive is reversible"). The dialog answers "did you mean to", the
  undo "I meant to and I was wrong", so both are defensible on an act that removes a policy from every
  list — but it is two steps, and no other archive has an undo. Keep both, drop the undo, or give every
  archive one. Discussed with the owner and left for now.

- Where the toolbar sits relative to tabs and the page header.
- Whether a disabled action explains itself, and how. Today the product has one Radix tooltip and
  ~40 native `title` attributes, which are invisible on touch and unannounced — and a disabled
  `Button` has `pointer-events-none`, so its `title` never fires at all. Still open in
  `analysis/ui/ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md` § 5.
- The `Export` control's shape (icon-only button vs menu item vs modal).
